Inclusion-minimality ensures every original cap occurs, so double counting proves the identity with three nonnegative summands. The repetition term bounds both the number of repeated caps and, by m≤2(m−1) for m≥2, the groups meeting a shared cap.

The union of the other groups proves the private-cap estimate. The strict threshold N>(h−1)(d+1) forces s=h. Under d≥h−1, hd≥(h−1)(d+1) verifies the other sufficient threshold. At h=4,d=2 and N=10,11,12 the counts are one, two, and three.

At N=12 both deficit terms for sizes and repetitions vanish, giving disjoint triples independently of normals. A minimal positive continuous-normal triple has a one-dimensional support kernel, hence rank two. More generally a deficient minimal positive group has k_g≤d and contributes at least one to the size deficit, so their number is at most Δ even if the other groups are arbitrary.

The original twelve-cap parallel-normal example is now consistent with the statement, which requires minimal positive dependence for the rank claims. The strict sub-M/9 budget implies N>9 by the union bound and still does not supply a group selection.

Checked f8a85d598f5eddb1 §§1 and 7. Minimality makes each original cap occur. Double counting incidences gives the three nonnegative deficit terms. The repetition term controls shared caps, and the inequality m≤2(m−1) for m≥2 controls the number of groups meeting a shared cap.
The other s−1 groups contain at most (s−1)(d+1) distinct caps, giving the private count. If N>(h−1)(d+1) then s=h. The implication from N>hd requires and uses d≥h−1.
For h=4,d=2, direct substitution gives private counts one, two, and three at N=10,11,12 and proves disjointness at twelve. The strict mass bound follows from subadditivity alone.

The conversion from size to continuous rank requires minimal positive dependence. The opening only assumes groups of bounded cardinality, which suffices for the incidence statements but cannot imply full continuous rank at N=12.

For a literal counterexample take twelve source points (z,x)=((j,j²),(0,0)) and caps 2i z₁−z₂+x₁≥i²−1/2. Each cap contains exactly its indexed point, by the squared difference identity. Four arbitrary triples meet the counting hypotheses with Δ=0 and all continuous normals equal (1,0).
